title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 293-296): Grothendieck is explicitly computing the 'non-oriented cartographic group for triangulated maps', written \tilde{\pi}'_{0,3} = \pi_1(Y, d_Y, Z/2Z; y). Here X is the Riemann sphere, more precisely U_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,\infty}. The group G is generated by the S_3 of anharmonic substitutions (\dot\sigma_0, \dot\sigma_1, \dot\sigma_\infty) and complex conjugation \dot\tau. The map f : X -> Y is the degree-6 quotient by S_3 (the j-line). \pi_1(X, G; x) is the G-equivariant (orbifold/stack) fundamental group of [X/G]. Its elements are pairs (g, homotopy class of a path from x to g x).

Previous page: the base point is y = -\bar{j} on Y. A lift x in f^{-1}(y) is chosen; that fibre has 6 points, 3 in each hemisphere. The choice is x in the spherical triangle (-\bar{j}, 0, 1/2). Three paths l'_0, l'_1, l'_\infty go from y to \tau y = -j along great-circle arcs, crossing the equator at 2, -1 and 1/2. Lifted, these give the three involutive generators of the extended (non-oriented) group.

This page lifts these arcs to X.
- They become paths \lambda_i from x to points z_i over \tau y. The \lambda_i run along edges of the barycentric subdivision of the double spherical triangles: the sides (1/2, \bar{j}), (\bar{j}, 0), (0, 1/2) of the triangle (0, 1/2, -\bar{j}).
- The endpoints are z_i = g_i x, with g_0 = \dot\sigma_\infty \dot\tau, g_1 = \dot\sigma_0 \dot\tau, g_\infty = \dot\tau. These are anti-holomorphic elements, i.e. reflections, matching the fact that each \tau'_i is an involution.
- So \tau'_i is the image in \pi_1(Y, d_Y, Z/2) of the pair (g_i, \lambda_i) in \pi_1(X, G; x).
- He then moves the base point to the habitual P = -\bar{j}, using a great-circle path l. This identifies \pi_1(X, G; x) with \pi_1(X, G; P) and rewrites (21): \tau'_i = (g_i, \lambda'_i), with \lambda'_i = g_i(l^{-1}) \circ \lambda_i \circ l a path from P to g_i P.
- The next page shows \lambda'_0 and \lambda'_1 are null-homotopic in U_{0,3} (the corresponding g_i are reflections fixing P), while \lambda'_\infty is the half great circle from P to \tau P.

Purpose: to express the generators of the non-oriented cartographic group explicitly inside the already-computed equivariant fundamental group of (P^1 - {0,1,\infty}, S_3 \times Z/2). This gives a presentation compatible with Galois/complex-conjugation actions. It is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' and is a bookkeeping step for Teichmüller-tower / Grothendieck–Teichmüller computations.
errors: Notational inconsistency in the first list of generators. g_0 = \dot\sigma_\infty\dot\tau and g_1 = \dot\sigma_0\dot\tau, yet he writes \tau'_0 = (\dot\sigma_0\dot\tau, \lambda_0) and \tau'_1 = (\dot\sigma_1\tau, \lambda_1). For the pairs to be well formed (\lambda_i a path from x to g_i x) the first component should be g_i. One of the two labelings has been permuted; he partly corrects this in (21), but (21) still carries the stray subscript '\dot\tau_0' and a dot missing on \sigma_0.

Minor: the NB locates the z_i in the triangles (-\bar{j}, 1/2, 1), (0, -\bar{j}, -1), (1/2, 0, -\bar{j}), whereas the crossed-out text on the next page lists different triangles. The precise placement is still being adjusted, but this does not affect the structure of the argument.

ideas.what: Elements of the fundamental group of a quotient [X/G] described as pairs (g, path from x to gx), and generators of an orbifold fundamental group obtained by lifting paths and recording the group element
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant fundamental group / orbifold (stack) fundamental group of [X/G]
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA1 and Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids of modular multiplicities); the explicit pair formalism appears in the Longue Marche manuscripts

ideas.what: Non-oriented triangulated cartographic group as \pi_1 of the j-line orbifold with complex conjugation, generated by three involutions lifted from reflections
ideas.modern_name: Extended modular group PGL_2(Z), i.e. the (2,3,\infty) extended triangle group, as cartographic group of non-oriented triangulated maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 (cartographic groups C_2, C'_2, triangulated variants)

ideas.what: Change of base point from x to the standard base point P = -\bar{j} via a great-circle path l, with \lambda'_i = g_i(l^{-1}) \circ \lambda_i \circ l
ideas.modern_name: Base-point change in equivariant fundamental groupoids

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine explicit computation: lifting generators of the extended (2,3,\infty) cartographic group to the S_3 \times Z/2-equivariant fundamental group of the thrice-punctured sphere. The underlying identification with PGL_2(Z) is well known (Jones–Singerman, Esquisse). The page contains no new result, only base-point bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'qui composent [?]' is uncertain; the sense is that the \lambda_i run along edges of the barycentric subdivision of the double spherical triangles.

'Nous allons utiliser le du grand cercle b/de -\bar{j} = P' should read roughly 'Nous allons utiliser le [chemin] l du grand cercle de [x à] -\bar{j} = P (précédemment habituelle pour le calcul de \pi_1(X, G))'.
'précédemment' is better read as 'point base précédemment habituel'.
In (21) the first component is written '\sigma_0 \dot\tau_0'; it is probably intended as the corresponding g_i (with a dot), the subscript on \tau being a slip.
Last line: 'de P = -\bar{j} vers g_i P respectivement'. The crossed-out alternative 'vers z_0, z_1, z_\infty' was replaced.
